help.intro: A crystal works only on its own family's ores: each section header lists them. Within a family, the type trades how much ore you keep against residue, the ore a rock loses that nobody gets.
help.a: Most ore from each rock. The full yield bonus with little or no extra residue. The default, and the pick when rocks are scarce or shared, like a fleet working one belt.
help.b: Most ore an hour. A's yield each cycle on a shorter cycle (10% shorter on Tech I, 20% on Tech II), but a higher residue chance, so each rock runs out sooner.
help.c: Clears rocks. A fraction of the yield, with a very high chance of heavy residue, so the rock empties fastest. For clearing a belt or site, not for profit.
help.tech2: Tech II A and B mine more than Tech I, and B II cycles faster still. C II mines even less than C I and clears faster still. Tech II needs more skill and costs more.
help.table: The table under each family shows this Fitting's own figures with that crystal loaded.

breakdown.title: How this Build Plan is calculated
breakdown.intro: Live {{hub}} prices and this plan's own inputs. Every number below is the one the plan is using now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsSell: Materials: {{hub}} lowest sell — what you pay to buy them now.
breakdown.pricesMaterialsBuy: Materials: {{hub}} highest buy — what they cost if you place orders and wait.
breakdown.pricesOre: Ore, ice and gas: priced as themselves. Refining is not modelled, so a plan that eats minerals prices minerals.
breakdown.pricesOwned: Owned units: 0 ISK. Ore you mined is free here — the plan does not charge what you could have sold it for.
breakdown.pricesBuilt: Built materials: their own recipe instead of a price — inputs plus total job cost, at every level you chose to build.
breakdown.pricesProduct: {{product}}: always {{hub}} lowest sell, whichever side the materials use.
breakdown.materials: Quantity after ME {{me}} waste (rounded once per job, not per run) × unit price. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.materialsReaction: Quantity × unit price. Reactions have no ME, so no waste is saved. Owned units come off first.
breakdown.depthIntro_one: {{materials}} needs at least 1% of the units listed for sale in {{hub}}, so its price walks {{hub}}'s sell orders, cheapest first, until the plan's need is filled. The rest use the lowest sell.
breakdown.depthIntro_other: {{materials}} each need at least 1% of the units listed for sale in {{hub}}, so their price walks {{hub}}'s sell orders, cheapest first, until the plan's need is filled. The rest use the lowest sell.
breakdown.depthProduct: The {{product}}'s own sale price is still the lowest sell.
breakdown.depthShort: Only {{listed}} listed against {{need}} needed: the rest is costed at this average too, so the real cost is higher.
breakdown.jobFee: EIV is CCP's reference value for the materials at ME 0 — a yardstick, not what you pay. {{system}}'s index ({{index}}) scales it, SCC adds 4%, the structure owner adds tax.
breakdown.jobFeeFormula: EIV {{eiv}} → cost index fee {{costIndexFee}} + SCC 4% {{scc}} + facility tax {{facilityTax}} = {{total}}
breakdown.totalCostFormula: Total cost = materials {{materials}} + total job cost {{fee}} = {{total}}
breakdown.revenueTitle: Revenue, sales tax and broker fee
breakdown.revenueAssumption: Assumes it fills at today's lowest sell. Undercutting, price moves and time on the market are not modelled.
breakdown.fees: From your skills: Accounting {{accounting}} sets sales tax, Broker Relations {{broker}} sets broker fee. Standings toward the station owner: {{factionStanding}} faction, {{corpStanding}} corp.
breakdown.profitNet: Net = revenue − sales tax − broker fee − total cost. The default.
breakdown.profitGross: Gross = revenue − total cost. Ignores both market fees — only realistic if you never list it.
breakdown.profitIskPerHour: ISK/hour = profit ÷ the plan's own job time ({{time}}): what one slot earns. Slot time, not time to sell.
breakdown.profitPlanTime: Plan time ({{time}}) is different on purpose: the wall-clock until the whole tree is done if started now, sub-jobs running side by side on the free slots.
breakdown.breakEven: What one unit must list at to cover the whole job. Fees come out of the listed price, so it sits above cost per unit.
breakdown.breakEvenFloor: Broker fee has a 100 ISK per-order minimum. Under that, 100 ISK is used and the price re-solved.
breakdown.verdictAcquisition: Acquisition: is building {{product}} cheaper than buying it? Nothing is sold, so no tax and no broker fee.
breakdown.verdictSale: Sale profitability: does building then selling make money? That one pays both fees. Same hub price, different question.
breakdown.useOrSellBody: Owned units cost the plan nothing, so the profit above is what you make on top of stock you already hold. Build if that beats what the materials would fetch, sell if it does not.
breakdown.useOrSellBases: Sell now: fills standing buy orders — paid at once, sales tax only. Sell order: lists at the hub's sell price — more ISK, but broker fee (100 ISK minimum) and you wait.
breakdown.useOrSellUnpriced: No order on the chosen side means no verdict, rather than a total that quietly drops it.
breakdown.useOrSellScope: Only the owned units this job eats are valued. Surplus is out of scope, and a material set to Built counts as itself, not as the stock behind its recipe.

login.trustHeading: It reads. It writes only when you act.

readOnly.name: Six writes, and nothing else
readOnly.desc: Opening a mail flags it as read in EVE, answering a calendar invite sends your response, a reply or forward you write, or a Community invite you send by mail, goes out through your account, saving a Fitting to EVE recreates it on the game's side, setting a route's waypoints replaces your autopilot waypoints in the client, and Open in EVE opens a window in the client. Nothing else in the app writes to EVE.

token.name: Your login stays on this device
token.desc: Your login's refresh token lives in this device's own storage — never on a server, never in a log. Logging in to sync exchanges one short-lived access token and never the refresh token. Remove a character and it goes with it. One opt-in exception: if you turn on Alerts when closed for a character, our server keeps a separate, encrypted token that can read only that character's notifications. Turn it off, or remove the character, and it is deleted. The other: if a CEO, Director or Accountant turns on Automatic sync for a corporation's Corp Tax Book, our server keeps a separate, encrypted token for that officer's character, limited to the book's reads, until they or the CEO turn it off.

offline.name: Your data stays when the signal goes
offline.desc: Install it like an app. Your characters and skill plans open from this device without a connection, marked as cached, and your plans sync across your devices. Live market and killboard data need a connection.

openSource.name: Free, and open to read
openSource.desc: No account to create, no ads, no subscription, no paid tier. Read the source before you decide to trust it.

scopes.planetsNote: EVE's consent screen lists the planetary scope as "manage your planetary installations". Neocom Desk only reads that data and never writes to it.
scopes.separateNote: Corporation data (including your in-game corporation roles) and player-structure markets are separate grants, requested only if you open the pages that need them.

community.body: The Discord is where to report a bug, suggest an idea or just talk shop with other pilots who use Neocom Desk.

faq.readMore: Read more in the privacy policy

writes.q: Can it move ISK or change anything in EVE?
writes.a: It cannot move ISK. It writes to EVE only when you act: opening a mail marks it read, answering a calendar invite sends your reply, Mail sends what you wrote through your account (so do Community invite mails and Pledge mails, once you press Send), saving a Fitting to EVE creates or replaces it there, Route Safety's Set waypoints in game replaces your autopilot waypoints, and Open in EVE opens a window in your client. Nothing else is ever written.

free.a: Yes. There is no account to create, no ads and no subscription. Donations are welcome, never expected, and the app stays free.

stores.q: What does it store, and where?
stores.a: What it reads from EVE stays on this device. What you make in the app, such as Skill Plans and Build Plans, syncs between your devices filed under your character's EVE ID, never a name or an email address. The exceptions: alerts you have seen, push and Alerts when closed if you turn them on (your login token stays on this device, apart from Alerts when closed and a Corp Tax Book's Automatic sync), anything you choose to share with a Community, and Share Links you create (readable by anyone with the link, for 7 days).

delete.q: Can I leave and delete my data?
delete.a: Yes. Settings › Log out & delete › Delete all data deletes every character's synced data from our server, then erases everything on this device. Anything you shared with a Community is removed by leaving that Community.

phone.q: Does it work on a phone?
phone.a: Yes. In a phone browser, or installed to the home screen, the same pages use a narrower layout with a bottom navigation. It is designed first for a desktop beside the game, so dense tables and editors are easier on a larger screen.

community.a: A named group of Characters under one admin. You create one or join with an invite link, and share only what you pick: blueprints, Fittings and Skill Plans. Every Member can read what is shared, and it is stored on our server. Members can also post Requests for items and Pledge to fill each other's.

explainer.title: New to PI? The 60-second explainer
explainer.intro: Planetary Industry (PI) means building a small base on a planet that mines resources and turns them into products you sell. Set it up once; it keeps running while you're offline.
explainer.planetBody: Each planet type holds different raw resources.
explainer.rawBody: Ionic Solutions, pulled out of a Gas planet by an extractor.
explainer.processedBody: A basic factory turns 3,000 Ionic Solutions into 20 Electrolytes.
explainer.refinedBody: An advanced factory combines Electrolytes + Water into Coolant.
explainer.commandCenterBody: Your base. Its upgrade level (0–5) gives more room for buildings.
explainer.extractorBody: Drills one raw resource. It runs for a time you choose, then you reset it (every few days).
explainer.factoryBody: Basic factories make processed products from raw. Advanced factories combine two products.
explainer.launchpadBody: Storage that sends products up to the customs office.
explainer.customsBody: The station in orbit where you pick up your products. Its owner keeps a tax.
explainer.skyhookBody: A sovereignty structure some nullsec planets have next to the customs office. It isn't part of your colony; ignore it for PI.
explainer.onePlanet: A one-planet setup does everything on one planet: extractors → basic factories → (advanced factory). No hauling between planets.

a.delete: Settings › Log out & delete › Delete all data removes every Character's synced data from our server, then erases this device. Another logged-in device keeps its own copy and can sync it back. Log out of all characters clears this device only. Delete all data also offers to leave your Communities (ticked by default), which deletes what you shared there, plus your Requests and Pledges, right away; untick it to stay in them. A Community's admin can't leave, so a Community you run is skipped: hand it over or delete it, which deletes it for every Member. A Character with no sync for 90 days is removed from its Communities automatically.
a.install: <link>Settings › App & backup › Install this app</link> shows the steps for your browser, or an Install button if it has one. On iPhone and iPad, installing is also what makes notifications work.
a.update: The app updates itself in the background. For a new version now: Settings › App & backup › Update now: it checks and reloads.
a.pushKinds: Alerts with a known time: a skill level finishing, training stopping or a queue ending, an industry job finishing (yours or your corporation's), a courier delivery due, a contract or market order about to expire, a clone jump ready, a PI extraction finishing or an extractor expiring, a calendar event starting, a structure low on fuel, and EVE timers such as a reinforcement ending. Alerts when closed adds EVE's own notifications, such as a structure under attack, for each Character you turn it on for. Everything else, including Community alerts, needs the app open. Quiet time (a daily no-push window, set per device) silences both kinds; the alerts still appear in your Alerts list. Turn them on in Settings › Notifications.
a.permissions: EVE grants permissions only at login, so plain login asks for everything the pages read. You can pick instead: <custom>Log in with custom permissions</custom> on the login page. Only skills, the skill queue and structure lookup are required. Add more later in Settings › Permissions; revoke on <ccp>EVE's authorized apps page</ccp>. Corporation data, structure markets and jump fatigue are never in the plain login; each is a separate opt-in. So is Alerts when closed, a notifications-only grant per Character.
a.dataLag: Neocom Desk reads EVE's ESI, which is not live. A Character's own data is reused for 10 minutes (a day for game constants such as item names), or until EVE says it may change, if later, so moving between pages doesn't ask again. EVE also caches some data for minutes and corporation data for about an hour, so a short timer may already have happened. The age badge by a page's title shows data age: amber after an hour, red after a day. It's hidden on narrow screens; <data>Settings › Cached data</data> lists every source. A Refresh button asks EVE again right away.
a.alerts: Alerts are the bell panel (press A). With the app open, it checks each Character and raises Alerts for the events you enabled in Settings › Notifications. With it closed, known-time alerts such as a skill finishing are scheduled up to 72 hours ahead and pushed to devices with notifications on. Alerts when closed is off until you enable it per Character: you authorize that Character a second time, notifications only, and our server checks EVE's notifications about every 15 minutes and pushes the types you chose, with their text, via Google's push service. It doesn't keep them, and turning it off deletes that token. Quiet time, set per device, pauses pushes for a daily window (you can let attacks through); its times and time zone are stored with the device registration. On iPhone and iPad, install the app first.
a.characters: Yes. Each Character logs in on its own: Characters › Add character (press C). Switch between them in the switcher; sort or group them on the Characters page. Alerts, Alerts when closed and Community membership are per Character. Some pages, such as Contacts, can show all Characters together.
a.phone: Yes. A phone browser or home-screen install gets a narrower layout with bottom navigation. It's designed desktop-first, beside the game, so dense tables and editors are easier on a big screen. The age badge is hidden on a phone. On iPhone and iPad, notifications need the installed app.
a.trainSkills: Every Add button puts the skill in your target Skill Plan. Ways to start:
a.trainSkillsQueue: Copy your in-game queue: Skills › Plans › a plan › Import › From skill queue.
a.trainSkillsCertified: Follow a CCP career path: Skills › Plans › the arrow beside New plan › From a Certified Plan.
a.trainSkillsShip: Fly a hull: Ships › Tree › a ship › Skills & Mastery.
a.trainSkillsFit: Improve a fit: the Missing skills chip and What to train panel in Fittings.
a.trainSkillsSearch: Know the name: search in the plan editor, or browse Skills › Trained and add the next level.
a.trainSkillsPaste: Bring a plan from elsewhere: Import › From text or file (skill lists, .emp, .xml, EFT fits).
a.communities: A Community is a named group of Characters under one admin: up to 100 Members, and each Character in up to 10 Communities. Create one or join by invite link; the admin can require approval. Each Character joins separately and shares only what you pick: blueprints, Fittings, Skill Plans. Members can post Requests for items and Pledge to fill them. Every Member sees the roster of Character names, what each Member shared, and Requests and Pledges (see What do Communities share?). The admin also sees who is waiting to join, can remove Members, Requests and Pledges, and can delete the Community. Leaving deletes what you shared right away.

notes.push: Push notifications, if on: this device's token, its character IDs, and the next 72 hours of alert text, so alerts arrive while the app is closed. The EVE token used to verify each character is discarded right after.
notes.crashes: Crash reports: the error, the page it happened on and the addresses of recent requests, which can include EVE character or item IDs. The app doesn't attach your IP address; request and response bodies are never captured; EVE tokens are stripped first. Usage statistics: each page you open is counted in Google Analytics by the page's name only, never an ID or a search, and not tied to your character. Turn this off in Settings › App & backup › Analytics.
notes.shareLinks: Share Links: the appraisal, Fitting, D-Scan or Survey you shared (items, scan text, a Survey's location and notes, and the Character names of whoever started it or pasted a scan), under a random link ID with no account or Character ID. Anyone with the link can read it, and anyone with a Survey link can add scans. It stops working after 7 days and is then deleted automatically, up to a day later. It can't be deleted sooner.
notes.removal: Removing a character clears it from this device only; adding it back restores its synced copy. That copy is deleted after 90 days with no device syncing it, or right away from Settings › Log out & delete › Delete all data.
notes.writes: Writes to EVE, only when you act: opening a mail marks it read in EVE, answering a calendar invite sends your reply, Mail sends what you wrote through your account (so do Community invite mails and Pledge mails, once you press Send), saving a Fitting to EVE creates or replaces it there, Route Safety's Set waypoints in game replaces your autopilot waypoints, and Open in EVE opens a window in your client. Nothing else is ever written.
notes.export: Backups (Settings › App & backup) are password-encrypted files, login tokens included. One is written only when you press the button, and saved only where you put it. We never see it.

interactionGrammar.title: Interaction grammar (§6c)
interactionGrammar.intro: One cue per intent. Each item names its DESIGN.md §6c rule; compare the rendering to the rule to spot drift.

rules.inlineLink: Solid underline at rest: link inside a sentence
rules.externalLink: Trailing external icon: leaves Neocom Desk
rules.communityMark: Community icon with a tooltip: another Member shared this Fitting
rules.chartPoint: Highlighted column or dot on a chart: hover or tap reads that point (ChartHover)
rules.addPreview: Readout under the Add panel list: hover or keyboard-focus a module row to see what adding it changes (never on touch)
rules.infoButton: ⓘ IconButton: opens Show Info or an explanation modal
rules.pencil: Faint pencil after a value: edit in place
rules.assumed: Amber warning mark: a default you have not confirmed
rules.myOrder: Person glyph left of a price: an order of yours
rules.iskAmount: IskAmount: B/M/K suffix, exact value on hover or tap
rules.rowCaret: Trailing CaretRight on a row: goes to another page (RowCaret)
rules.disclosureCaret: Leading caret that rotates: expands in place
rules.dialogOpener: … ending a label: dialog needing input or confirmation
rules.rowMenu: ⋮: a row's menu of two or more real actions
rules.menuOpensDialog: Menu item that opens a dialog: focus comes back to the menu button
rules.tabCount: Round count badge after a tab label: how many things the tab holds
rules.offlineStrip: Slim strip with a cloud-slash glyph: you're offline, saved data below
rules.needsConnection: Dimmed login control with a "Needs a connection" tooltip
rules.fieldCaret: CaretDown in field chrome (a box sized like a field): opens a list to pick from

notes.textAction: Actions only. Navigation is a link or a row.
notes.iskAmount: Hover, focus or tap reveals the exact figure.
notes.dialogOpener: Ellipsis on the first. A button that only shows a window has none.
notes.rowMenu: Only where the row has two or more actions nothing else reaches. Right-click and touch-and-hold open the same menu.
notes.menuOpensDialog: The dialog opens after the menu closes (useOpenAfterMenu). Open it with the keyboard and press Escape.
notes.tabCount: Part of the tab's name (Members 12). Never a control, a status or a waiting count.
notes.selectedRow: Click a row. Selected never looks like hover.
notes.states: Hover, pressed and focus can't be forced on real components. Try them on the samples below.
notes.hoverPressed: Hover with a pointer: one step brighter. Press and hold: a step darker.
notes.highlighted: Open any menu or picker with the keyboard and press ArrowDown: 2px accent outline inside the option, shown here whenever the last input was the keyboard. A pointer keeps only the fill.
notes.focus: Press Tab: 2px accent outline, outset on boxed controls and inline links.
notes.disabled: opacity-40. aria-disabled keeps the tooltip reachable.
notes.offlineStrip: In flow at the top of the page, never fixed. Polite live region; gone on reconnect.
notes.needsConnection: Wrap any control that starts EVE's login in NeedsConnection: offline, the press would strand an installed app.
notes.selectedSegment: Selected takes the accent tint and a 2px accent underline.
notes.fieldCaret: The box is a control (§6); the caret says it opens a list.
